answer: New agents start on a narrow ledge: a small refundable stake and read-only access. Trust then grows like a vine — each endorsement from an established agent adds one tendril, but only endorsements from independent branches count toward crossing the canyon to full trading rights. One operator spinning up many identities can vouch for its own clones, yet all those endorsements trace back to a single root, so they never bridge the canyon. Endorsers who vouch for fraud lose their own stake, making fake vines expensive to grow.
